$about: The cited pull request is OPEN, not merged: GitHub Actions was in a major outage while this round ran (jobs never got a runner and cancelled at 15 minutes), so its CI could not go green and nothing was merged on a check that never fired. Both observations were re-verified against that branch's tree, not against main, and a later round re-runs them against whatever main carries then - which is exactly the rule that a cited fix is not a verified fix. 2026-08-06, drift-honesty round: the two severe findings about the drift NUMBER meaning less than it appears to - GREEN-02 (drift 0 on a repo that has specified nothing) and STACK-04's core-side half (a missing tool scored as repository drift, and a compliance check with install side effects) - re-run against the current tree before anything was changed, on the rule that a finding is open only while it still reproduces. Both reproduced, with exact numbers. Both are addressed here; one is closed and re-verified, one is half-closed and stays on the punch list, because its remaining half is a one-line declaration in the Layer 2 stack repo and no core change can make it for that repo. The observations keep the 2026-08-04 round's target label so they supersede those findings there. One 2026-08-04 claim did not survive re-measurement and is corrected in the evidence rather than quietly inherited.

observations.evidence: Reproduced first against the unmodified tree, by the case's own procedure: a raw copy of `standard/` with `specs/capability-map.json` removed (it is fill-from-repo, so a degit'd tree carries none) reported `drift 3 - 96% adopted (75/78)`; writing `.standards-version` took it to `drift 1 - 99% (77/78)`; adding `"profile": "core"` to the carried manifest left `drift 1 - 99% (68/69)`; writing an empty `specs/capability-map.json` produced `self-verify: OK - drift 0 - 100% adopted (69/69), 0 excepted - compliant with the standard`, exit 0, with zero capability specs written and five WARN lines saying the shipped templates were still shells. The 2026-08-04 figures (94% 46/49, then 98% 40/41, then 100% 41/41) differ only in denominator - the manifest has grown since - and the defect is the same one: the number was correct and the sentence was not. Fixed by reporting rather than forbidding, and the choice is the finding's substance. Scoring the absence would put drift 0 out of reach of an honest greenfield for the whole length of the walk: greenfield.md step 1 scaffolds and promises `Empty but valid: self-verify passes`, step 6 writes the first spec, and a gate nobody can clear between them is one everybody learns to route around - the same reasoning the placeholder scan already runs on. `self-verify.mjs` now walks `specs/` for capability specs (`specs/<capability>/<file>.md`, the shape spec-structure.mjs holds them to, excluding templates, READMEs and the engine's ephemeral plan/tasks/checklists) and, when there are none, raises one WARN and appends the caveat to the drift-0 verdict itself: `OK - drift 0 - 100% adopted (69/69), 0 excepted - compliant with the standard - AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CLAIM: no capability spec exists here yet, so this says the repo is shaped like the standard, not that any behaviour has been specified under it`. Re-verified by re-running the identical procedure on the fixed tree: same drift 0, same exit 0, caveat present. Held in both directions by three cases in `tools/self-verify-drift-test.mjs`: the empty tree still reaches drift 0 and carries the caveat; one real `specs/booking/spec.md` (with a roster persona, so the run is a genuine drift 0 rather than the caveat trading places with a structure failure) clears it; a `specs/booking/` holding only `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `README.md` does not clear it. Checked adversarially rather than assumed: with the caveat's condition short-circuited to false and the manifest hashes regenerated so nothing else moves, exactly those two of the three go red - the third asserts an absence and is there to catch the check firing when it should not.

Half closed, half not, and the split is not effort - it is which repo owns the remaining line. HALF ONE, the number, reproduced exactly and is fixed. A fixture carrying a `stack.manifest.json` whose only guard is `pnpm check:all`, run with pnpm removed from PATH, reported `self-verify: drift 1 - 99% adopted (78/79), 0 excepted - 1 required entry is unmet`, exit 1. The same fixture with the guard rewritten to the merged stack-side form (an explicit `pnpm not on PATH` message) reported the identical verdict line - the stack-side fix improved the message and left the number untouched, which is what left this open. Measured against a genuine failure rather than asserted: a guard that ran and exited 1 with `checked 214 files: 3 lint errors` printed the same string, character for character (`identical verdict line: true`). `self-verify.mjs` now resolves a guard's prerequisites before `execSync` and reports one that cannot run as NOT RUN - a `SKIP` row, counted as neither drift nor adoption, named in the verdict line - so the two now read `drift 0 - 100% adopted (78/78) ... 1 CHECK NOT RUN HERE (stack-check-all)`, exit 0, against `drift 1 - 99% adopted (78/79)`, exit 1. That is a loosened gate and is treated as one: a missing tool used to exit 1 and no longer does, so `OK` is dropped from the verdict whenever a check did not run - the exit code answers whether the repo complies, and a check that never started has no opinion on that, but the word a reader skims must not say the run was complete. This needs nothing declared: any bare word in `run` that is no shell builtin and resolves nowhere on PATH is inferred, so today's shipped node manifest gets the legible answer without changing. HALF TWO, the side-effect install, has a mechanism and no consumer. Core cannot know that `pnpm check:all` installs anything, so the only honest fix is a guard declaring what it needs: `requires: [{ "kind": "path", "match": "node_modules" }]` now stops the guard executing at all. Demonstrated both ways on one fixture with pnpm's `verify-deps-before-run=install`: undeclared, `self-verify` ran the guard and left a populated `node_modules` behind (INSTALLED AS A SIDE EFFECT: true); declared, the guard was not run, nothing was installed, and drift was unchanged at 0. But `repository-standards/node`'s shipped `stack.manifest.json` declares no `requires`, so against the stack as it stands a machine with pnpm and no `node_modules` still runs the guard and can still install. That line belongs to the stack repo and cannot be written from here, so this stays a fail rather than becoming a `partial` that would drop off the punch list while the behaviour it names is still reachable. CORRECTION TO THE 2026-08-04 EVIDENCE, published rather than inherited: that round recorded the install as unconditional (`Packages: +376... Done in 3.2s`). Re-measured, it is configuration-dependent. On pnpm 10.33.0 with this machine's default config the guard did not install - with and without a lockfile present, `pnpm check:all` failed with `sh: biome: command not found` and `node_modules` stayed absent. With `verify-deps-before-run=install` it installed on the spot (`Packages: +2 ... Done in 167ms`, the same shape as the original `+376 ... 3.2s`). So the side effect is real and reproducible, and it is not the default everywhere; the fix is worth having either way, because a compliance check whose behaviour depends on a package manager's local setting is not a compliance check. Seven cases in `tools/self-verify-drift-test.mjs` hold this half, each asserted in both directions and each verified by reverting the engine and re-running with the manifest hashes regenerated so nothing else moves: neutralising the prerequisite resolver turns three red (absent tool, declared path prerequisite, malformed requires entry), restoring the unconditional `OK` prefix one, and reading `a || b` as two requirements rather than a fallback one. The self-review pass that produced those numbers also caught its own first attempt: the `OK`-prefix assertion was written against a fixture sitting at drift 1, where the drift-0 line never prints and the assertion could not have failed whatever that line said.
